transcript:
incident-bot: ALERT: high OOM rate observed in cluster rw-inference-prod (node-pool: us-west-2a). 18 distinct containers restarted in last 12m. Autotriage: probable KV cache fragmentation + paging pressure. Incident ID INC-2026-732
maria: saw the alert, digging into node logs now. customers complaining about tail latencies > 5s on chat endpoints.
aj: ack. i'm oncall. @maria can you paste the top container ids?
maria: quick list:
```
container rw-srv-7f9d8 / pod rw-paged-abc-7f9d8
container rw-srv-3a2c1 / pod rw-paged-def-3a2c1
container rw-srv-11f22 / pod rw-paged-ghi-11f22
```
maria: kubectl logs for rw-paged-abc shows repeated CUDA OOM and then container exit loop:
```
E 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
W 2026-03-15T10:12:03Z allocator: page_alloc_fragmentation: resident=12.3GB cached=6.4GB slots=... 
I 2026-03-15T10:12:04Z kvcache: attempted evict 0 entries, fragmentation=0.78
F 2026-03-15T10:12:05Z process: exiting with code 137
```
kevin: fragmentation 0.78 is high. Looks like slow drift where kvcache loses contiguous slabs and paging rate increases until OOM.
devon: any customer-facing impact metrics? which routes affected?
aj: from Grafana: increased 500s on /v1/chat/generate and high retry rate on host rw-api-1. Downstream latency spike primarily for seq_len > 2048.
maria: also saw a node flap in cluster: kubelet restarted on n-07 due to oom_kill of runtime-worker.
ops-bot: Notified paging team pagerduty PD: @paging-team
kevin: quick mitigation: reduce per-request batch_size to 1 for paged-attn worker pool and enable aggressive kvcache eviction (set env KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.2). That should free ~1-2GB per node.
aj: can we patch prod quickly? what's the safe path to avoid rolling all pods at once?
devon: plan: 1) mark pool draining state for canary routing; 2) apply small runtime config change to k8s Deployment with rollingRestart maxUnavailable=10%; 3) route small percent traffic to fallback non-paged model (v2-medium) until stable.
maria: applying config change now to canary set (deployment rw-paged-canary). running:
```
kubectl set env deployment/rw-paged-canary KVCACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.2 --namespace=prod
kubectl set env deployment/rw-paged-canary MAX_BATCH=1 --namespace=prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/rw-paged-canary --namespace=prod
```
kevin: also add a temporary eviction job to compact slabs on other nodes: `redwoodctl runtime compact-slabs --selector=pool=paged-attn --dry-run=false`
aj: please wait for canary health checks. if canary OK, we'll promote.
incident-bot: Canary deployment rw-paged-canary restarted. Health check status: pending.
maria: canary passed 3/3 health probes after restart. memory resident dropped ~1.8GB on that pod.
devon: good. start slow promotion: increase traffic weight to 10% for the non-paged fallback route; reduce paged pool traffic by 20%.
aj: doing traffic shift in routing console now. also enabling a circuit-breaker: route to fallback on any instance returning CUDA OOM or 5xx for >3 requests in 2m.
kevin: pushing an emergency config to runtime so kvcache periodically scans and defrags on low-traffic windows: KVCACHE_DEFRAG_PERIOD=60s (temp). This is a bit heavy but okay short-term.
maria: note: logs still show one pod with repeated page faults and libc++ errors; I'm putting that node in maintenance to avoid noisy restarts.
ops-bot: Node n-07 cordoned and pods evicted. Replacement node spin-up in progress.
aj: customer impact: Support dashboard shows ~12 customers saw degraded responses in last 30m; 2 have open support tickets. Not seeing data loss, just increased latencies and a couple of timeouts.
devon: escalate to infra for potential driver issue if OOMs persist after compaction. ticket created: INFRA-911, pinging @infra-lead.
kevin: troubleshooting note: our paged-attn allocator uses a slab size that doesn't play nice with some CUDA allocation patterns when fragmentation >70%. We should consider a long-term fix: adaptive slab merging + kvcache slot reclamation.
aj: for now, keep the temporary mitigations for next 2 hours, monitor error rate and memory resident. If stable, we'll revert KVCACHE_DEFRAG_PERIOD to normal value.
maria: adding metrics to incident channel: links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/oom-paged
- Traces: https://traces.internal/redwood/trace/INC-2026-732
- Logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/prod?q=rw-paged
incident-bot: Alert severity: High -> Reduced to Medium after canary success. Keep watchers: @devon @kevin @aj @maria @paging-team
devon: handing off to morning shift SRE at 07:30 PT. Please include runbook steps and current state in the handoff note. I'll open a follow-up RFC for allocator changes.
aj: current state summary for handoff: mitigations applied (kvcache evict threshold, max_batch=1, defrag period), canary healthy, node n-07 cordoned, traffic partially routed to fallback. Customer impact reduced, 2 support tickets open. Monitor for 1 hour before full promotion back.
maria: I'll update the incident doc and add the exact commands we ran. leaving the thread in case more flaps occur.
kevin: follow-up action items:
- A: schedule allocator RFC with benchmarks (owner: kevin)
- B: improve kvcache telemetry and ragged-slab alerts (owner: maria)
- C: consider smaller slab sizes for paged-attn runtime (owner: eng-runtime)
- D: add emergency runtime knobs to console for faster mitigation (owner: devon)
aj: thanks all. i'm marking this thread as 'oncall-handoff'. will escalate if OOMs reappear.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-732 updated: status=monitoring, pagerduty cleared.
maria: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
